Matt — thanks again for taking time yesterday. As discussed, ACME is evaluating a 24-month private offer and is motivated by an accelerated commit profile in year 1 (larger up-front consumption vs steady monthly). A few follow-ups so we can model the economics and confirm channel implications: 

- Can you confirm the expected FY1 consumption curve (months 1–6 and 7–12)? The spreadsheet you mentioned would be great.
- ACME’s procurement team flagged they need a clear channel pass-through percentage to the reseller (CloudPilot) for invoicing and tax treatment. They asked for a line item in the PO that shows the reseller commission separately. What pass-through % do we propose?
- Finance will need to see net revenue to Redwood post-pass-through for ARR recognition. I’ve attached a baseline worksheet and a draft terms sheet (v2 PDF).

Next steps: if you send the consumption estimate I’ll run two scenarios (standard net pricing vs. accelerated-commit uplift) and mark the channel breakouts. Planning to share back by EOD Thursday.

Cheers,

Looping in Connor for ops/finance thought. Quick internal reaction:

- 18% pass-through is high relative to our baseline commission assumptions for CloudPilot (we usually model 10–12% for cloud marketplace resellers). If we accept 18%, net Redwood revenue drops materially and will impact the discount we can offer.
- If ACME is accelerating spend, we could offer a time-limited accelerator credit (e.g., additional 5% rebate applied to months 1–6) instead of increasing the base discount — preserves channel margin but gives ACME the economics they want up-front.
- Need Laura to confirm any marketplace listing constraints (billing visibility for pass-through line) and whether Redwood can legally accept a PO showing the reseller line separately while invoicing net.

Ben

Ben / team — brief ops notes after checking with billing/legal:

- We can support a PO that shows a reseller pass-through as a separate line, but Redwood needs an accompanying "reseller commission agreement" (simple one-pager) that CloudPilot countersigns to validate the commission flow. This is for audit and tax.
- Billing can invoice ACME net of the pass-through, but we must preserve gross list-price and the commission line in our internal revenue ledger for ASC/IFRS reconciliation. Finance will need mapping fields from the PO (line IDs).
- Marketplace constraints: on GCP and AWS private offers the seller PO can include separate line descriptions, but Azure Marketplace sometimes aggregates — if ACME wants Azure we need to flag potential limitations.

I’ll draft the reseller one-pager and share. Connor, can you run the two scenarios Ben mentioned and add an ARR recognition line (net to Redwood) — we’ll need that for legal and ACME Finance.

—Laura

Attached are the two model outputs: scenario A (standard discount with 12% reseller pass-through) and scenario B (accelerated credit approach with 12% pass-through + 5% months 1–6 accelerator). Key takeaways:

- Scenario A (12% pass-through): Redwood net ARR = $8.7M over 24 months; up-front effective cash is more even across months.
- Scenario B (accelerator): Redwood net ARR = $8.9M over 24 months; gives ACME ~6% extra effective upfront economy in months 1–6 and preserves a lower base pass-through for the partner.
- If we accept 18% pass-through, Scenario B net ARR falls to $8.1M and requires ~3% additional base list discount to keep ACME at target TCO.

I recommend proposing Scenario B with an explicit CloudPilot commission at 12% and a 5% accelerator rebate applied to months 1–6 (rebate paid as a credit on invoice). This keeps the channel commission reasonable and gives ACME the up-front economics they want.

Connor O'Brien
Deal Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
